- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

214	# Gradient checkpointing (activation recomputation) is enabled for all models
215	# by default — it trades a recompute in backward for a large activation-memory
216	# saving, which matters for the deep/long-context grokking runs. It is applied
217	# per transformer/SSM block and is automatically bypassed in eval (no grad) so
218	# validation/inference cost is unchanged. Override per-run via the "grad_checkpoint"
219	# config key.
220	def _maybe_checkpoint(module, x, enabled):
221	    """Run `module(x)`, optionally under activation checkpointing.
222	
223	    Only checkpoints when training AND grad is being tracked — under
224	    torch.no_grad()/eval there is nothing to recompute so we call directly,
225	    avoiding checkpoint's overhead and its "no input requires grad" warning.
226	    """
227	    if enabled and module.training and torch.is_grad_enabled():
228	        return _grad_checkpoint(module, x, use_reentrant=False)
229	    return module(x)

294	# ── Data 1: Modular Division (a ÷ b) mod p  [Decoder] ────────────────
295	def make_data(p=97, frac_train=0.5, val_ratio=0.10, seed=42):
296	    rng = random.Random(seed)
297	    op_tok, eq_tok = p, p + 1
298	    pairs, labels = [], []
299	    for a in range(p):
300	        for b in range(1, p):
301	            b_inv = pow(b, p - 2, p)
302	            pairs.append([a, op_tok, b, eq_tok])
303	            labels.append((a * b_inv) % p)
304	    c = list(zip(pairs, labels)); rng.shuffle(c)
305	    pairs, labels = zip(*c)
306	    n_train_total = int(len(pairs) * frac_train)
307	    n_val = int(n_train_total * val_ratio)
308	    n_train = n_train_total - n_val
309	    x = torch.tensor(pairs, dtype=torch.long)
310	    y = torch.tensor(labels, dtype=torch.long)
311	    return x[:n_train], y[:n_train], x[n_train:n_train_total], y[n_train:n_train_total], x[n_train_total:], y[n_train_total:]
312	
313	# ── Data 2: MNIST-Addition (a + b) mod p  [ViT] ──────────────────────
314	def make_mnist_addition_data(p=97, frac_train=0.5, val_ratio=0.10, seed=42):
315	    import torchvision
316	    from torchvision import transforms
317	    transform = transforms.Compose([transforms.Resize((14, 14)), transforms.ToTensor()])
318	    mnist = torchvision.datasets.MNIST(root='./data', train=True, download=True, transform=transform)
319	    digit_images = {d: [] for d in range(10)}
320	    for img, label in mnist:
321	        digit_images[label].append(img.squeeze(0))
322	    rng = random.Random(seed)
323	    number_images = {}
324	    for n in range(p):
325	        tens, ones = n // 10, n % 10
326	        img_t = digit_images[tens][rng.randint(0, len(digit_images[tens]) - 1)]
327	        img_o = digit_images[ones][rng.randint(0, len(digit_images[ones]) - 1)]
328	        number_images[n] = torch.cat([img_t, img_o], dim=1)
329	    pairs, labels = [], []
330	    for a in range(p):
331	        for b in range(p):
332	            pairs.append((a, b)); labels.append((a + b) % p)
333	    combined = list(zip(pairs, labels)); rng.shuffle(combined)
334	    pairs, labels = zip(*combined)
335	    n_train_total = int(len(pairs) * frac_train)
336	    n_val = int(n_train_total * val_ratio)
337	    n_train = n_train_total - n_val
338	    images = []
339	    for a, b in pairs:
340	        full = torch.cat([number_images[a], number_images[b]], dim=0)
341	        patches = full.unfold(0, 7, 7).unfold(1, 7, 7).contiguous().reshape(16, 49)
342	        images.append(patches)
343	    x = torch.stack(images); y = torch.tensor(labels, dtype=torch.long)
344	    return x[:n_train], y[:n_train], x[n_train:n_train_total], y[n_train:n_train_total], x[n_train_total:], y[n_train_total:]
345	
346	# ── Data 3: Sequential Chained Division  [Mamba] ─────────────────────
347	def make_sequential_division_data(p=97, chain_length=3, frac_train=0.5, val_ratio=0.10, seed=42):
348	    rng = random.Random(seed)
349	    op_tok, eq_tok = p, p + 1
350	    target_size = p * (p - 1)
351	    seen = set(); pairs, labels = [], []
352	    while len(pairs) < target_size:
353	        a = rng.randint(0, p - 1)
354	        bs = tuple(rng.randint(1, p - 1) for _ in range(chain_length))
355	        key = (a, *bs)
356	        if key in seen: continue
357	        seen.add(key)
358	        result = a
359	        for b in bs: result = (result * pow(b, p - 2, p)) % p
360	        seq = [a]
361	        for b in bs: seq.extend([op_tok, b])
362	        seq.append(eq_tok)
363	        pairs.append(seq); labels.append(result)
364	    combined = list(zip(pairs, labels)); rng.shuffle(combined)
365	    pairs, labels = zip(*combined)
366	    n_train_total = int(len(pairs) * frac_train)
367	    n_val = int(n_train_total * val_ratio)
368	    n_train = n_train_total - n_val
369	    x = torch.tensor(pairs, dtype=torch.long); y = torch.tensor(labels, dtype=torch.long)
370	    return x[:n_train], y[:n_train], x[n_train:n_train_total], y[n_train:n_train_total], x[n_train_total:], y[n_train_total:]

374	    vr = c.get("val_ratio", 0.10)
375	    if mt == "decoder":  return make_data(p, ft, vr, seed)
376	    elif mt == "vit":    return make_mnist_addition_data(p, ft, vr, seed)

380	# ── Model 1: Decoder Transformer ─────────────────────────────────────
381	class DecoderBlock(nn.Module):
382	    def __init__(self, d, h, seq_len=4):
383	        super().__init__()
384	        self.attn = nn.MultiheadAttention(d, h, dropout=0., batch_first=True)
385	        self.n1 = nn.LayerNorm(d); self.n2 = nn.LayerNorm(d)
386	        self.ff = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(d, 4*d), nn.GELU(), nn.Linear(4*d, d))
387	        self.register_buffer('causal_mask', torch.triu(torch.ones(seq_len, seq_len, dtype=torch.bool), 1))
388	    def forward(self, x):
389	        a, _ = self.attn(x, x, x, attn_mask=self.causal_mask)
390	        x = self.n1(x + a); return self.n2(x + self.ff(x))
391	
392	class Transformer(nn.Module):
393	    def __init__(self, nl=2, d=128, h=4, ntok=99, seq=4, grad_checkpoint=True):
394	        super().__init__()
395	        self.tok = nn.Embedding(ntok, d); self.pos = nn.Embedding(seq, d)
396	        self.layers = nn.ModuleList([DecoderBlock(d, h, seq_len=seq) for _ in range(nl)])
397	        self.norm = nn.LayerNorm(d); self.out = nn.Linear(d, ntok)
398	        self.register_buffer('pos_ids', torch.arange(seq).unsqueeze(0))
399	        self.grad_checkpoint = grad_checkpoint
400	    def forward(self, x):
401	        h = self.tok(x) + self.pos(self.pos_ids)
402	        for l in self.layers: h = _maybe_checkpoint(l, h, self.grad_checkpoint)
403	        return self.out(self.norm(h)[:, -1, :])

405	# ── Model 2: ViT ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
406	class EncoderBlock(nn.Module):
407	    def __init__(self, d, h):
408	        super().__init__()
409	        self.attn = nn.MultiheadAttention(d, h, dropout=0., batch_first=True)
410	        self.n1 = nn.LayerNorm(d); self.n2 = nn.LayerNorm(d)
411	        self.ff = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(d, 4*d), nn.GELU(), nn.Linear(4*d, d))
412	    def forward(self, x):
413	        a, _ = self.attn(x, x, x)
414	        x = self.n1(x + a); return self.n2(x + self.ff(x))
415	
416	class ViT(nn.Module):
417	    def __init__(self, p=97, patch_dim=49, num_patches=16, d=128, h=4, nl=2, grad_checkpoint=True):
418	        super().__init__()
419	        self.patch_proj = nn.Linear(patch_dim, d)
420	        self.cls_token = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(1, 1, d) * 0.02)
421	        self.pos = nn.Embedding(num_patches + 1, d)
422	        self.layers = nn.ModuleList([EncoderBlock(d, h) for _ in range(nl)])
423	        self.norm = nn.LayerNorm(d); self.out = nn.Linear(d, p)
424	        self.register_buffer('pos_ids', torch.arange(num_patches + 1).unsqueeze(0))
425	        self.grad_checkpoint = grad_checkpoint
426	    def forward(self, x):
427	        B = x.size(0); h = self.patch_proj(x)
428	        h = torch.cat([self.cls_token.expand(B, -1, -1), h], dim=1)
429	        h = h + self.pos(self.pos_ids)
430	        for l in self.layers: h = _maybe_checkpoint(l, h, self.grad_checkpoint)
431	        return self.out(self.norm(h[:, 0, :]))

434	class SelectiveSSMLayer(nn.Module):
435	    def __init__(self, d, state_dim=16, dt_rank=None, expand_factor=2):
436	        super().__init__()
437	        self.state_dim = state_dim; self.d_inner = d * expand_factor
438	        self.dt_rank = dt_rank or max(d // 16, 1)
439	        self.in_proj = nn.Linear(d, self.d_inner * 2, bias=False)
440	        self.conv1d = nn.Conv1d(self.d_inner, self.d_inner, kernel_size=3,
441	                                padding=1, groups=self.d_inner, bias=True)
442	        self.x_proj = nn.Linear(self.d_inner, self.dt_rank + state_dim * 2, bias=False)
443	        self.dt_proj = nn.Linear(self.dt_rank, self.d_inner, bias=True)
444	        A = torch.arange(1, state_dim + 1, dtype=torch.float32)
445	        self.A_log = nn.Parameter(torch.log(A.unsqueeze(0).expand(self.d_inner, -1)))
446	        self.D = nn.Parameter(torch.ones(self.d_inner))
447	        self.out_proj = nn.Linear(self.d_inner, d, bias=False)
448	        self.norm = nn.LayerNorm(d)
449	    def _selective_scan(self, x, dt, B, C):
450	        batch, L, _ = x.shape; A = -torch.exp(self.A_log); dt = F.softplus(dt)
451	        # Try CUDA kernel
452	        if x.is_cuda:
453	            try:
454	                from mamba_scan_ext import selective_scan_cuda
455	                return selective_scan_cuda(
456	                    x.contiguous(), dt.contiguous(),
457	                    B.contiguous(), C.contiguous(), A.contiguous()
458	                )
459	            except ImportError:
460	                pass
461	        # Python fallback
462	        h = torch.zeros(batch, self.d_inner, self.state_dim, device=x.device, dtype=x.dtype)
463	        ys = []
464	        for t in range(L):
465	            dt_t = dt[:, t, :].unsqueeze(-1)
466	            h = torch.exp(dt_t * A.unsqueeze(0)) * h + (dt_t * B[:, t, :].unsqueeze(1)) * x[:, t, :].unsqueeze(-1)
467	            ys.append((h * C[:, t, :].unsqueeze(1)).sum(-1))
468	        return torch.stack(ys, dim=1)
469	    def forward(self, x):
470	        residual = x; xz = self.in_proj(x); x_main, z = xz.chunk(2, dim=-1)
471	        x_main = F.silu(self.conv1d(x_main.transpose(1, 2)).transpose(1, 2))
472	        x_dbc = self.x_proj(x_main)
473	        dt, B, C = x_dbc.split([self.dt_rank, self.state_dim, self.state_dim], dim=-1)
474	        y = self._selective_scan(x_main, self.dt_proj(dt), B, C)
475	        y = self.out_proj((y + x_main * self.D.unsqueeze(0).unsqueeze(0)) * F.silu(z))
476	        return self.norm(y + residual)

543	    def __init__(self, threshold=0.95, max_steps=20_000, patience=500, metric_name="test_acc"):
544	        self.threshold=threshold; self.max_steps=max_steps; self.patience=patience
545	        self.metric_name=metric_name  # which accuracy feeds step(): "test_acc" or "val_acc"
546	        # [A4-M1/M2] best_metric_acc / metric_acc are metric-agnostic names: under
547	        # val-stopping this tracks val, under test-stopping it tracks test — the
548	        # old test_acc-specific names mislabelled the val-criterion runs.
549	        self._triggered=False; self._counter=0; self.best_metric_acc=0.
550	        self.grokking_step=None; self.grokking_wall=None; self._t0=time.time()
551	        self.stopping_reason=None; self.stopping_step=None
552	    def step(self, metric_acc, current_step):
553	        if current_step >= self.max_steps:
554	            if self.stopping_reason is None:
555	                self.stopping_reason="max_steps"; self.stopping_step=current_step
556	            return True
557	        self.best_metric_acc = max(self.best_metric_acc, metric_acc)
558	        if metric_acc >= self.threshold:
559	            if not self._triggered:
560	                if torch.cuda.is_available(): torch.cuda.synchronize()
561	                self._triggered=True; self.grokking_step=current_step
562	                self.grokking_wall = time.time()-self._t0
563	            self._counter += 1
564	            if self._counter >= self.patience:
565	                if self.stopping_reason is None:
566	                    self.stopping_reason=f"{self.metric_name}_threshold"; self.stopping_step=current_step
567	                return True
568	        else: self._counter=0
569	        return False

903	    wgmma megakernel) for an L3-REAL cell. Model-GENERIC: fires for whichever of
904	    (transformer_decoder|vit|mamba × <wgmma-wired optimizer>) is registered on this

912	    update — real model math, real optimizer math, ZERO intermediate launches.
913

915	    There is NO eager fallback left. ALWAYS returns the training LOSS (a float,
916	    mean cross-entropy) on success; on ANY condition that the old code would have
917	    declined to eager for (fusion off, not an L3-REAL cell, AMP on, unwired
918	    precision, stale ABI) it RAISES RuntimeError rather than silently downgrading.

920	    ran (dispatch.cpp has no silent fallback: a wgmma request runs wgmma or throws),
921	    so the path report is the real executed path, not the requested one.

1770	        seed_data = {}

1773	            task = task_queue.get()

1	"""Runtime hardware detection for the fused kernel architecture.
2	
3	Detection is **arch-honest**: ``detect_arch()`` / ``get_gpu_arch()`` report the
4	REAL device architecture, not a collapsed vendor selector. An A100 reports
5	``sm_80``, an L40S ``sm_89``, an H100 ``sm_90a`` — they are NOT all flattened to
6	``90``. AMD reports its real ``gfx<...>`` target; TPU reports ``tpu_v6e``.
7	
8	    NVIDIA: sm_70 / sm_75 / sm_80 / sm_86 / sm_89 / sm_90a / sm_100a / ...
9	    AMD:    gfx906 / gfx908 / gfx90a / gfx942 / gfx950 / gfx110x / ...
10	    TPU:    tpu_v6e
11	
12	The C++ extension is still built as a multi-arch fat binary (one impl per
13	vendor family; see setup.py), so the *fat-binary impl selector* is a separate
14	concern from the reported arch. ``normalize_arch()`` maps a real arch to its
15	impl-family selector (NVIDIA → 90, AMD → 942, TPU → "tpu_v6e") for the code
16	paths that load the matching per-SM/-gfx code from the fat binary. Reporting
17	stays honest; only the binary loader normalises.
18	
19	Feature predicates (``supports_fp8`` etc.) are keyed to the REAL compute
20	capability via ``get_device_sm()``. ``FORCE_ARCH`` accepts any real arch form
21	(``sm_80``, ``gfx942``, ``tpu_v6e``, or a bare numeric CC like ``80``/``90``).
22	"""

38	# Replaces ad-hoc print()s and is the channel for arch-detection / ops-
39	# resolution diagnostics. We attach a NullHandler so importing the package
40	# never configures the root logger (library-friendly); the level is only
41	# applied when the env var is set, so default behaviour is quiet.

71	# by profile.MODELS and the CLI. Canonical names ("mamba3",
72	# "transformer_decoder", "vit") are the identifiers used by the
73	# megakernel engine, fused cells, and C++ dispatch. canonicalize_model()
74	# is the ONLY place this mapping is defined.

78	    "mamba": "mamba3",
79	    "decoder": "transformer_decoder",

81	    # Canonical names map to themselves (idempotent).
82	    "mamba3": "mamba3",

97	    canonical names ("mamba3", "transformer_decoder", "vit") are the megakernel/
98	    fused-cell identifiers. This function accepts either form and returns the
99	    canonical form. Raises ValueError for unknown names.

105	            f"Accepted: {sorted(_MODEL_CANONICAL.keys())}"

122	    "sm_70", "sm_75", "sm_80", "sm_86", "sm_89",

138	    """Raised when the detected arch is not one of {sm_90, gfx942, tpu_v6e}."""

161	        return 'hip'

173	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
174	# Arch detection

177	# Real NVIDIA compute capabilities the package recognises, in ascending
178	# order, mapped to their canonical arch-label spelling. A device CC is
179	# resolved to the highest label it is >= to (so a future sm_91 still resolves
180	# to the sm_90a kernel family, never silently dropping to fp32).
181	_NVIDIA_CC_LABELS = (
182	    (70, "sm_70"), (75, "sm_75"), (80, "sm_80"), (86, "sm_86"),
183	    (89, "sm_89"), (90, "sm_90a"), (100, "sm_100a"), (103, "sm_103a"),
184	    (120, "sm_120a"),

188	def _sm_to_arch_label(cc: int) -> str:
189	    """Map a real NVIDIA compute capability int to its canonical arch label.
190	
191	    Honest: an A100 (CC 80) → ``sm_80``, an L40S (CC 89) → ``sm_89``, an H100
192	    (CC 90) → ``sm_90a``. A CC above the highest known entry resolves to that
193	    highest label (forward-compatible), a CC below the lowest raises.
194	    """
195	    label = None
196	    for threshold, name in _NVIDIA_CC_LABELS:
197	        if cc >= threshold:
198	            label = name
199	    if label is None:
200	        raise UnsupportedArchError(
201	            f"NVIDIA compute capability {cc} is below the minimum supported "
202	            f"(sm_70).")

206	def _normalize_force_arch(force: str) -> Union[int, str]:
207	    """Map a FORCE_ARCH string to the REAL arch it names (honest).
208	
209	    Returns a real arch label (``sm_80``/``gfx942``/...) or ``tpu_v6e``. A bare
210	    numeric value is treated as an NVIDIA compute capability and resolved to its
211	    real label. Raises on unrecognised input. Use :func:`normalize_arch` on the
212	    result when an impl-family selector (90/942) is needed.
213	    """
214	    if force.startswith('tpu'):
215	        return "tpu_v6e"
216	    # AMD: any gfx target. Honor the exact gfx label; the bare ``942`` form maps
217	    # to gfx942 for back-compat.
218	    if force.startswith('gfx'):
219	        return force
220	    if force == '942':
221	        return "gfx942"
222	    # NVIDIA: sm_* label (normalise the bare ``sm_90`` alias to ``sm_90a`` etc.)
223	    if force.startswith('sm_'):
224	        try:
225	            cc = int(force[3:].rstrip('a'))
226	        except ValueError:
227	            raise UnsupportedArchError(
228	                f"FORCE_ARCH={force!r} not recognized.") from None
229	        return _sm_to_arch_label(cc)
230	    if force.startswith('sm'):
231	        try:
232	            cc = int(force[2:].rstrip('a'))
233	        except ValueError:
234	            raise UnsupportedArchError(
235	                f"FORCE_ARCH={force!r} not recognized.") from None
236	        return _sm_to_arch_label(cc)
237	    # Bare numeric compute capability (e.g. ``80`` for A100, ``90`` for H100).
238	    if force.isdigit():

242	        f"(sm_70..sm_120a or a numeric CC), an AMD arch (gfx906..gfx1201), "
243	        f"or tpu_v6e.")

246	def normalize_arch(arch: Union[int, str]) -> Union[int, str]:
247	    """Map a real arch to its fat-binary impl-family selector.
248	
249	    NVIDIA labels (``sm_*``) and bare CC ints → ``90``; AMD ``gfx*`` (and the
250	    bare ``942``) → ``942``; ``tpu_v6e`` → ``"tpu_v6e"``. This is the ONLY place
251	    the NVIDIA→90 / AMD→942 collapse happens, and it is used solely by the code
252	    that loads the matching per-arch code from the multi-arch fat binary — never
253	    for *reporting* the device's real arch.
254	    """
255	    if arch == "tpu_v6e":
256	        return "tpu_v6e"
257	    if isinstance(arch, int):
258	        return 942 if arch == 942 else 90
259	    if arch.startswith('gfx'):
260	        return 942
261	    if arch.startswith('sm'):
262	        return 90
263	    raise UnsupportedArchError(f"Cannot normalize unknown arch {arch!r}")

275	    or the vendor is unknown.

452	# Loads the per-arch specialized C++ extension. Raises on first kernel
453	# attribute access if the extension isn't built — there is no Python
454	# fallback path, but `import grokking_optimizers` succeeds either way so
455	# that profiling / tooling code can introspect the package without a

460	class _LazyOps:
461	    """Lazy proxy for the compiled `grokking_optimizers._ops` extension.
462	
463	    Resolves on first attribute access. `hasattr(_ops, "foo")` correctly
464	    returns False when the extension isn't built; direct attribute access
465	    raises AttributeError with a descriptive build hint. This preserves the
466	    no-fallback contract (kernels are unreachable without a build) while
467	    allowing import-time introspection.
468	    """
469	    __slots__ = ("_real", "_error", "_attr_cache")
470	
471	    def __init__(self):
472	        object.__setattr__(self, "_real", None)
473	        object.__setattr__(self, "_error", None)
474	        # Memoize resolved kernel attributes so repeated `_ops.fn` access on
475	        # the hot path skips the module getattr after the first lookup.
476	        object.__setattr__(self, "_attr_cache", {})
477	
478	    def _resolve(self):
479	        if self._real is not None:
480	            return self._real
481	        if self._error is not None:
482	            return None  # cached failure
483	        try:
484	            import importlib
485	            real = importlib.import_module("grokking_optimizers._ops")
486	            object.__setattr__(self, "_real", real)
487	            return real
488	        except ImportError as e:
489	            object.__setattr__(self, "_error", e)
490	            logger.debug("grokking_optimizers._ops not importable "
491	                         "(extension unbuilt?): %s", e)
492	            return None
493	
494	    def __getattr__(self, name):
495	        if name.startswith("_"):
496	            raise AttributeError(name)
497	        cache = self._attr_cache
498	        cached = cache.get(name)
499	        if cached is not None:
500	            return cached

500	            return cached
501	        real = self._resolve()
502	        if real is None:
503	            raise AttributeError(
504	                f"grokking_optimizers._ops.{name}: C++ extension not built. "
505	                f"Run `pip install -e .` (supported arches: {SUPPORTED_ARCHES}). "
506	                f"Original ImportError: {self._error}"
507	            )
508	        attr = getattr(real, name)
509	        cache[name] = attr
510	        return attr
511	
512	    def bind(self, name):
513	        """Resolve ``name`` once and return the underlying kernel callable.
514	
515	        Callers (optimizers) cache the returned bound function on the instance
516	        so subsequent steps skip the proxy ``__getattr__`` entirely. Raises the
517	        same descriptive error as attribute access if the extension is unbuilt.
518	        """
519	        return self.__getattr__(name)
520	
521	    def __bool__(self):
522	        return self._resolve() is not None
523	
524	    def __repr__(self):
525	        real = self._resolve()
526	        if real is None:
527	            return f"<_LazyOps unbuilt: {self._error}>"
528	        return f"<_LazyOps wrapping {real!r}>"
529	
530	
531	_cached_ops = _LazyOps()
532	
533	
534	def get_ops():
535	    """Return the lazy `_ops` proxy. Never raises at call time."""
536	    return _cached_ops

551	def has_kernels() -> bool:
552	    """True iff the compiled C++/CUDA/HIP kernel extension is importable AND
553	    exposes the fused optimizer kernels.
554	
555	    This is the honest capability flag (spec §6a): the optimizers have NO
556	    pure-PyTorch fallback for ``.step()`` — they hard-require this extension and
557	    a GPU. Gate any GPU-only code on ``grokking_optimizers.has_kernels()``
558	    instead of assuming a fallback exists. Returns False on a CPU-only / unbuilt
559	    install (import still succeeds for introspection/tooling).
560	    """
561	    ops = _cached_ops
562	    if not ops:
563	        return False
564	    return any(hasattr(ops, name) for name in _KERNEL_PROBE_NAMES)

1031

1034	    bc2 = 1 - beta2**step from the shared step counter. One (bc1, bc2) pair is
1035	    correct because the race steps every parameter together (the megakernel treats
1036	    each flat param as one task; see opt_components.cuh FusedScalars note).

1039	    optimizers consume are set; the rest keep their inert ABI defaults).

1513	                     targets, *, state_cache, step, return_grad=False,
1514	                     gemm_impl="wgmma",
1515	                     lr=None, betas=None, weight_decay=None, eps=None):
1516	    """Run ONE TRUE L3 fused TRAIN step (real fwd+bwd+opt) for an L3-REAL cell.
1517	
1518	    PHASE 1+2: for an L3-REAL cell ((transformer_decoder|vit|mamba3, adamw)) this
1519	    REPLACES the eager forward + backward + optimizer.step() with ONE persistent
1520	    megakernel that runs the REAL model forward+backward AND the AdamW update —
1521	    real model math, real optimizer math, ZERO intermediate kernel launches (the
1522	    owner rejected CUDA graphs; this is the chosen path). The caller MUST therefore
1523	    NOT run its own forward/backward/step for this cell; it uses the LOSS this
1524	    returns for logging.
1525	
1526	    The input path is carried through the existing ``ops.fused_step`` ABI (whose
1527	    pybind arity is pinned), packed PER MODEL into the single ``input`` tensor:
1528	      * int_tokens (decoder/mamba): ``input`` = int32 [B*(per+1)] = tokens[B*per]
1529	        ++ targets[B]  (per = seq: decoder 4, mamba 8).  ``tokens`` is [B, per].
1530	      * float_patches (vit): ``input`` = float32 [B*(per+1)] = patches[B*per] ++
1531	        targets BIT-REINTERPRETED into the trailing float slots (per = 16*49 = 784;
1532	        ``tokens`` here is the float patch tensor [B, 16, 49]). The targets are
1533	        carried via ``tensor.view(torch.int32)/view(torch.float32)`` bit-reinterpret
1534	        (NOT a value cast) so they are lossless for ALL int32 — dispatch.cpp reads
1535	        them back with reinterpret_cast<const int*>. This mirrors the decoder's
1536	        int pack: one contiguous ``input`` tensor.
1537	    ``params`` = the flat concat of ``named_parameters()`` (in order); ``state`` =
1538	    [m|v|extra] (3*total) + a trailing loss slot the kernel writes the mean
1539	    cross-entropy into. We read that slot back and return it.
1540	
1541	    State/params ownership (critical): the megakernel updates the FLAT param
1542	    buffer in place, so we keep BOTH the flat param buffer AND the [m|v|extra|loss]
1543	    state in ``state_cache`` (keyed by the model id), allocated ONCE and reused —
1544	    reallocating per step would reset momentum and the run would never grok. After
1545	    the kernel we scatter the updated flat params back into the live
1546	    ``p.data`` (named_parameters() order), so the model carries the new weights for
1547	    the next eager eval.
1548	
1549	    Args:

1564	            against the oracle. Default False (the race only needs the loss).

1567	            megakernel; "wgmma" → the bf16 tensor-core launcher (decoder/vit only;
